prediction:
THOUGHT: The infant has signs of lower intestinal obstruction — progressive abdominal distension, tympanitic abdomen, and crying with palpation — with plain abdominal x‑ray showing dilated bowel and absence of rectal gas, indicating distal obstruction. The barium enema demonstrates a transition zone in the distal colon, which is the classic radiographic finding of a distal aganglionic segment. Normal inflammatory markers and absence of systemic signs make infectious or ischemic causes less likely. Differential diagnoses such as intussusception, volvulus, or meconium ileus are less consistent with the imaging and age of presentation; the transition zone on contrast enema strongly points to congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells. Confirmation would be by rectal suction biopsy showing absence of ganglion cells, and the condition is classically Hirschsprung disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon). 
DIAGNOSIS: Hirschsprung disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon)
